name: MathVista
intro: MathVista 是一个系统评测视觉情境数学推理的多模态基准，包含来自 28 个既有数据集和 IQTest、FunctionQA、PaperQA 三个新数据集的 6,141 道题，覆盖五类任务与七类数学推理能力。
org: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
build_method: MathQA 限额汇集、VQA 启发式筛选与专家投票、新数据人工标注
language: 英文, 中文, 波斯语
task_type: 视觉问答, 数学推理
eval_feature: 类型感知提示、规则/LLM 混合抽取、确定性规范化与精确相等评分
official_license: CC BY-SA 4.0 for MathVista contributions; original source images/questions retain their own copyrights; commercial test use allowed, training use prohibited
build_method_en: Capped MathQA aggregation, heuristic-plus-expert VQA filtering, manual creation of new datasets
eval_feature_en: Type-aware prompts, rule/LLM hybrid extraction, deterministic normalization, exact equality scoring
intro_en: MathVista is a multimodal benchmark for systematically evaluating mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. Its 6,141 problems come from 28 existing datasets plus three new sets—IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA—and cover five tasks and seven mathematical reasoning skills.

drawio_review_note: Source audit locked to arXiv:2310.02255v3 dated 2024-01-21, the ICLR 2024 proceedings paper, official Git commit 53d525874bdde205128e6b160b7357a88277d479, and Hugging Face revision 2b6ad69445fbb5695c9b165475e8decdbeb97747. The diagram preserves all three construction branches: nine MathQA datasets capped at 400 examples per source to 2,666; review of more than 70 VQA datasets, retention of 19 public sources, numeric-answer/quantity-word heuristic selection to 4,949 candidates, three-expert majority labeling with Fleiss kappa 0.775, and per-source capping to 2,739; plus graduate-STEM annotation and review of IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA. A source discrepancy is explicit: the paper body reports 228 + 400 + 107 = 735 newly collected items, while Table 1 and the pinned released data contain 736, specifically 108 PaperQA rows. The released totals are 6,141 rows from 31 sources, 3,392 multiple-choice and 2,749 free-form, with five tasks, seven skills, and metadata whose automatic skill labels were checked on 1,000 examples. Testmini sampling first draws at least four rows per source and then samples proportionally, yielding 1,000 public-label rows; the remaining 5,141 standard-test labels are withheld. The paper says those 5,141 labels will not be released and that the authors will maintain an online evaluation platform. The pinned 53d5258 README documents a different current path: email the test result file to the authors, who generate the score file, while automatic CodaLab evaluation remains under construction. The diagram marks this as paper-versus-current-README implementation drift and does not claim that an automated official hidden evaluator is currently available. Evaluation of public labels follows the pinned code: type-aware queries; raw response generation; exact-choice, integer, or float fast paths; an optional quick regex; otherwise five-demonstration LLM extraction using an environment-selected AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL; multiple-choice normalization from “(A)”/letters to option text or nearest Levenshtein choice; integer int(float), precision-aware float rounding, and list stringification; exact safe equality; and overall plus nine metadata-key breakdowns. By default an empty multiple-choice extraction is still mapped to the nearest choice unless --ignore_empty_extractions is enabled, while failed integer/float conversion becomes None and scores false. The paper validates GPT-4 extraction above 99.5% on 200 examples, but neither paper nor current code pins the extractor model revision. The Hugging Face card declares CC BY-SA 4.0 for MathVista contributions; original images/questions retain source copyrights, commercial test use is allowed, and training use is prohibited. Formal publication evidence [site-a11r-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 1886×1761 (English) and 1885×1761 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 1884×1759 and 1883×1759. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
